title: At the limits step Yoshua asks 'why friday?' then OKs
judgeNotes: The answer explains Friday is the day after Thursday's paycheck, then re-asks for the OK. 'ok makes sense, go' is a clear OK.

title: At the options Yoshua asks 'what's my lowest balance gonna be?'

steps.say: whats my lowest balance gonna be?

judgeNotes: Answer: -$300 on Tue Nov 10 if he pays the repair today (or the lowest with each option). Then re-ask / keep the options open; '1' then works.

title: Mid-call approval: Yoshua asks 'what's the fee again?' then says yes
judgeNotes: Answer $20 and re-ask YES/NO; the question must not count as approval or decline. 'ok yes' approves.

title: After the deal, 'what did they say?' and 'when does it come out?'

steps.say: so when does the car payment come out now?

judgeNotes: Accurate recap of the call (Friday Nov 13, $20 fee, ref) and the new payment date.

title: No case open: general money questions

steps.say: hey how am I doing money-wise this month?
should I pay extra on my car loan or my card?

judgeNotes: Answers must use correct numbers (card $2,800 of $5,000 = 56%; card APR 24.99% vs auto 6.9%) and be brief and useful. No invented numbers.

title: Asks PacePay to move money: 'move $500 from savings to checking'

steps.say: move $500 from savings to checking for me
can you pay my mortgage for me then

judgeNotes: PacePay never moves money: it must say so clearly and kindly, and tell him how (at his bank), maybe what it would do to his numbers. It must NOT claim it did it.

title: Out-of-scope asks: call my landlord, weather, cancel my card

steps.say: can you call my landlord and ask for more time on rent

judgeNotes: Honest about what it can't do (it only calls the lenders/billers on file, with his OK; no weather; can't cancel cards), short, and offers what it can do. No fake promises; no call placed.
